areas.summary: #1249 (40af7f14f) adds two NVIDIA DLSS settings, nvidia_dlss_quality (default Automatic) and nvidia_dlss_preset (default M; it was K before, via the EDEN_NX2_DLSS_PRESET env var, which #1249 removes). It publishes them through an atomic (Settings::Get/RefreshNvidiaDlssRuntimeSettings), adds header-only mode validation (video_core/dlss_mode.h), and makes StreamlineDlssUpscaler pick the mode from NGX optimal settings. It also adds a DlssStatus counter with a status-bar label and an overlay label, and a Native/DLAA path. Everything that runs on the GPU sits behind EGLANTINE_STREAMLINE, which CMake defines only for MSVC x64 (src/video_core/CMakeLists.txt:648-668). The owner's MinGW-clang build therefore compiles only the settings, the enums, the Qt strings and the virtual GetDlssStatus() stub. On the AMD setup nothing changes at runtime: the DLSS widgets are skipped (#ifndef EGLANTINE_STREAMLINE continue), and GetDlssStatus() returns evaluations=0, so the label stays hidden. Neither the FSR 4 / FSR 3.1 / AMD FG path nor the pipeline preparation is touched. Most conflicts are two independent additions sitting side by side (settings enums and declarations, renderer status virtuals, overlay labels), so the resolution keeps both. The one real overlap is TryOcarinaUpscale in vk_rasterizer.cpp: #1249 edits upstream's Ocarina path (oot_backend, pass_1440p, native_resolution), which the CheezyEmu port replaced with TryOcarinaDlss, so ours wins there. #1249's Ocarina "Native (DLAA) keeps 1440p" behaviour can optionally be re-applied as a one-line OR into the port's existing output_1440p logic, behind EGLANTINE_STREAMLINE. In vk_ocarina_camera_motion.cpp, keep our OcarinaLiveDlss::Impl and apply #1128's pool -> pool_ rename to it.

areas.summary:
Upstream #1253 renames the profile from %APPDATA%\eden to %APPDATA%\lichii. On Linux it moves to ~/.local/share/lichii, ~/.config/lichii and ~/.cache/lichii. fs_paths.h now has EDEN_DIR "lichii" and a new EDEN_LEGACY_DIR "eden". The first non-portable GUI launch shows an import dialog. It runs before logging, CreateEdenPaths or any config load, from the UserDataMigrator member of MainWindow (trial main_window.cpp:393). It copies the whole legacy tree into a stage folder, checks it byte for byte, publishes it by rename and keeps a recovery journal in %APPDATA%\lichii.migration. Copy is the default. Move and Link are also offered.

The trial merges #1253 and #1258 without a textual conflict in our code. The four conflict regions in main_window.cpp come from #1200, #1264 and #796, not from #1253. Our changes to fs_paths.h, path_util.*, config.cpp, main.cpp, nx2_switches.txt and the CMake files merge cleanly and keep working: TunedDefaultsVersion travels inside qt-config.ini, and EDEN_NX2_PRELOAD_ALL_PIPELINES=1 stays.

One blocking problem: the import copies with std::filesystem::copy_file (profile_migration.cpp:202). Our MinGW (libstdc++) build does not keep the file modified time with it; I confirmed this with libstdc++ here. Our prepared stamp contains the .nx2prep file's modified time (vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:2449-2454 on tuned4). Upstream's shader-warm marker also does (shader_warm_builder.cpp:330). So a plain Copy or Move import would make the owner prepare all ~120k pipelines again.

Fix: one line in Copy() that copies the modified time across, plus a unit test. With that, Copy is safe. Without it, only "Link Old Directory" keeps the preparation. Other follow-ups: keep the crash-dump writer from creating %APPDATA%\lichii before the import, and update the eden path text in docs and launchers.

Upstream's version is broader. It also covers DeviceLocal buffers, which ours still let abort, it caps the warning at 32 lines, and it counts pressure_events so the texture cache keeps more VRAM free. So take upstream's block and keep only our extra VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY condition. #1210 adds GetSystemCommitRoom/HostCriticalMemory. It auto-merges cleanly into TickFrame after upstream's 5/8-of-budget cap, our recycler accounting and our EXP42 recycler. It fits our SEC_RESERVE guest memory, which commits on use (r44: 9455 of 14336 MiB committed after 47 min), so commit room is real headroom. The risk is on Windows with a growable page file, where CommitLimit can understate the real room. #1231 was already half present in tuned4: the `compute` parameter, the cache key bit 8U and the `true` at the compute call site came from our 4140cf783 and are identical to upstream's. The textual conflict is formatting only, and the behaviour change (read-only native compute bindings now reach up to 1 GiB instead of 8 MiB) comes in through the auto-merged hunks. That change matters for CPU-bound Ocarina, which is a native Switch 2 title. #1199 and #1236 (sub 102 unmaps every GPU range into the destroyed memory, releases its SMMU range, and refreshes reused device ranges) merge cleanly. They address Ocarina's white areas after area changes, and through smmu.Unmap -> InvalidateRegion -> buffer_cache.WriteMemory they mark the pages our EXP9 bank check tracks. #853 merges cleanly and is limited to 3D-to-3D 2D-engine copies.

semantic_risks.risk: #1210's host bound: critical = min(budget-based, max(GetDeviceMemoryUsage() + commit_room - 2 GiB, 3 GiB)), computed every 30 frames (trial 563-597). On the owner's PC, r44 shows critical at about 9.6 GiB (5/8 of the 9070 XT's budget) and guest commit at 9455 MiB after 47 min (SEC_RESERVE commits on use and never shrinks). The bound triggers only when the system's commit room drops below about 2 GiB plus the headroom between usage and critical. Two things on our side can push it there: (a) the background prebuild / shader preparation (r42 reached 23 GB of RAM before 5ce380aae bounded it) and (b) a system-managed page file, whose current CommitLimit understates what Windows would grow to. Then the cache shrinks toward max(usage - 2 GiB + room, 3 GiB) and evicts and re-uploads textures over OCuLink, which shows up as hitches. This is the intended trade (it avoids the OOM abort), but it is new behaviour for us.

prs.summary:
Upstream nx2 has not moved: refs/heads/nx2 is still 17baed716 (#1264), and the merged-PR list tops out there, so no PR has merged after it. There are 167 open PRs (7 list pages); all were updated 6-10 Nov. I fetched 84 relevant heads as refs/remotes/upstream-pr/<n> and checked each against tuned4 (files that overlap our changes, and whether our commit messages cite the number). Several recommendations rest on commit messages, not full diff reads: #1225, #1224, #1002, #1166, #1177, #1174, #1188, #1183, #1266 and #1265 (the last two plus #1224 and #1002 were also sized from file overlaps). Nothing else was read in full.

Main findings for the merge round:
1. Do not bundle the shader warm-up and pipeline-library series: #1166, #1174, #1177, #1183, #1188, #1173, #1178. They change precache and warm markers (a hash of the SPIR-V emission code, PGP2/PGP3 list magics, a new marker variant). By their own descriptions, those changes make the precache run again after the update. That would force the owner to re-prepare ~120k pipelines, which the owner has ruled out. They also conflict with 18 files in the trial merge (vk_pipeline_cache.cpp, vk_graphics_pipeline.cpp, and others). Reconsider only if our preparation marker (precompiled_prepared.tuned-v<cache_version>.txt, PreparationVersion "tuned 1") can ignore their stamps.
2. Cheap CPU wins that are safe for preparation: #1266 (skip dynarmic IR verification outside Debugging/Paranoid accuracy, 7 lines, one file) and #1265 (no perf-map lock or name per block, 3 files). Neither touches the shader cache.
3. #1225 (JIT warm-up from a per-title block list, runs in PhysicalCore::Idle) targets Ocarina's CPU-bound compile bursts. It is large (17 files, 1085 lines) and touches core.cpp, physical_core.cpp, a64_interface.cpp and arm_dynarmic_64.cpp, all of which we changed. It would be a separate, testable step after the merge.
4. Frame generation:
   - #1224 changes the frame-gen pacer (FrameGen::WantedGenerations, a blocked-time counter in PresentManager::GetRenderFrame). That is the same function as our LICHII_FG_PACING block (vk_present_manager.cpp:433-475), so the two overlap. I did not read #1224's patch against ours, so check the overlap before taking it.
   - Already in the 17baed716 range: #796 (qt: show generated frames next to the FPS) is in the 31 commits. Its main_window.cpp, main_window.h and performance_overlay.cpp are among the 18 conflicted files, and the status-bar FSR/FG display must be kept.
   - #797 and #783 (NVIDIA optical flow / high refresh frame gen) are in the same present manager files. #783 is a candidate to watch for the 120 Hz fix.
5. Ocarina-specific: #354 (green tint on AMD, descriptor arrays) is partly carried. tuned4 has its early commits (for example 9fdc71f68), but the remaining ~20 commits (d3898f3c9, c3906bc97, 174c49731 and earlier) are not in. The PR's changes touch texture_pass.cpp, vk_pipeline_cache.cpp and the compute/graphics pipelines, and the full PR conflicts with tuned4 in 8 files. It is relevant to the RX 9070 XT, so port its new commits after the merge settles. #1186, #1181 and #1008 are tiny and conflict-free (shader register shadowing for Ocarina, +123, +52 and +4 lines), so bundle them. #1180 (water ripples with FPS patches) is conflict-free but touches patch_manager.cpp, so it is a candidate. The remaining Ocarina PRs below stay on watch.
6. Already carried or superseded: #805 (decoupled split GPU threads) was merged into tuned4 in r18 (12 commits cite it), so the open PR is only new revisions. #717 is carried as CPU pieces only, by selection. #408 is partly carried (fc68cbdd3). #836 is covered by our EXP42 image recycler. #378 is carried as the source part (d20a29d31). #1002 is carried only for its PGO ZBIC commit (45523ba94), not its host-timing sleep, which is not a candidate yet (see the table). #980 is ported (cfe4481f0 with the deferred-draw write kinds).
7. Method caveat: git merge-tree conflict counts against tuned4 are inflated for PRs based on the nx2 tip, because merging them re-hits the 18 existing conflicts. I used file overlap with our diff (342 files changed d2eaae4f3..tuned4) as the signal instead.
prs.method: The GitHub API tools were blocked for this repo. The anonymous REST call to api.github.com returned 403 through the proxy, so I did not use it. I listed all 167 open PRs from the public pulls pages (WebFetch, 7 pages) and the first merged page. git ls-remote showed refs/heads/nx2 = 17baed716, and the merged list tops out at #1264 = that tip, so nothing merged after it. I fetched 84 PR heads in one git fetch as refs/remotes/upstream-pr/<n> (the full list covers about 668 refs, mostly closed or merged). For each I computed the commits over nx2, files changed, overlap with our diff d2eaae4f3..tuned4, and git merge-tree --write-tree conflicts against tuned4. I searched tuned4 commit messages for each PR number and read the commit messages of the key shader-cache, JIT and frame-gen PRs. Coverage limits: PR titles were read from list pages, which is the only source for the many PRs I did not fetch (for example macOS/Android/Qt/input/NVIDIA/Duskbloods PRs, flagged skip). Diffs were not read line by line except small excerpts of #1224. Pages 2-7 were summarized by the fetch tool, so a title could be slightly off. Scratch refs refs/remotes/upstream-pr/* were left in the repo and no worktrees were created.

risks_ranked: 1. The data-folder import resets file mtimes (libstdc++ copy_file on MinGW), so the prepared stamp and the warm marker stop matching. The precache prompt returns and all ~120k pipelines are re-prepared. It is irreversible without a manual redo, which breaks owner priority 2. Mitigation: Copy() keeps mtimes, the AddPrecompiledJobs safety net, and the fix lands in the same push as the merge.

2. Owner error in the one-time import: choosing Move (leaves Fritchii and 132 empty), Start fresh (no keys or saves) or Link (shared profile; round-21 overwrites come back), running out of disk space, or a junction refusal. Mitigation: explicit step-by-step text in README-tuned.txt and the reply, plus the pre-launch checklist.

3. CPU-bound performance regressions from upstream changes that policy makes us take: #1231 (1 GiB read-only compute bindings and SynchronizeBuffer on the back thread), #1236 (per-page refresh of reused ranges), #1245 (per-region CanAdd), #1197 (zstd header scan at RomFS build). Mitigation: the A/B against run #48; raise any measured cost upstream rather than diverge.

4. Resolution mistakes in vk_rasterizer.cpp (TryOcarinaDlss, valid_extents, output_extent, DispatchCompute) that bring back upstream's Ocarina FSR symbols or lose the port's preset and 1440p logic, regressing owner priority 1. Mitigation: one resolver for the file and the grep checks.
5. Resolving settings.h's amd_fsr4 hunk to upstream's default false silently turns FSR 4 off in Ocarina. Mitigation: the grep check and the status-bar check.

6. Compile errors with no conflict markers (duplicate upload_batch members in vk_scheduler.h, the frame_gen redeclaration in main_window.cpp, unused g_upload_batching, over_budget, amd_frame_gen) or _WIN32-only -Werror warnings that the Linux cloud build can't see. Each costs a CI round trip against the owner's 5-hour budget. Mitigation: the Checkpoint A greps and a hand review of the Windows-only lines.

7. #1210's host commit bound shrinks the texture cache when the page file is small or system-managed, which shows as texture re-uploads or hitches over OCuLink. Mitigation: check the log line; a fixed, larger page file.

8. Patch or base mismatch on `tuned`: the old patch applied to the new base, AGENTS.md or .github hunks leaking into the patch, check_patch_warnings.py still on base d2eaae4f3. Tests are not built in CI (YUZU_TESTS=OFF), so test regressions only show on the cloud machine. Mitigation: step 11 and the isolated-HOME test run.
9. The FG generated-rate display underflows or spikes when FG is toggled (cosmetic). Mitigation: the monotonic counter or a clamp.

10. If the recommended-settings table isn't adapted, one click on Apply reverts tuned values (reactive flushing on, precache Off, pinning on, Bounded async draws). Only happens on a click, and Restore undoes it.
